content.text:
Map each node in every diagram on the provided canvas to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change any diagram’s text or the canvas layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

54	pub const List = DoublyLinkedList(Node);

    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   240	    inline fn metadata(self: *const Node) *const Page {
   241	        return switch (self.data) {
   242	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   243	            .compressed => |*page_| &page_.page,
   244	        };
   245	    }
   246	
   247	    const RestoreMode = enum {
   248	        /// Decode the compressed representation back into the raw mapping.
   249	        preserve,
   250	
   251	        /// Discard the compressed representation without decoding it. The
   252	        /// caller must not read the page contents before overwriting them.
   253	        discard,
   254	    };
   255	
   256	    /// Restore this node to the resident representation.
   257	    ///
   258	    /// Preserve mode reconstructs the page contents and is used by `page`.
   259	    /// Discard mode skips decoding for callers which will overwrite or destroy
   260	    /// the page. Both modes recommit the retained mapping, free the encoded
   261	    /// allocation, and leave the node in a valid resident state.
   262	    noinline fn restore(self: *Node, comptime mode: RestoreMode) *Page {
   263	        const compressed = switch (self.data) {
   264	            .resident => |*page_| return page_,
   265	            .compressed => |*page_| page_,
   266	        };
   267	
   268	        // Decommit only discarded the physical pages. Recommit prepares the
   269	        // still-reserved mapping for decoding or reuse by the caller.
   270	        terminal_mem.recommit(compressed.page.memory);
   271	
   272	        const restored = switch (mode) {
   273	            .preserve => compressed.restore() catch |err| {
   274	                // Compressed nodes retain the immutable encoding and exact
   275	                // output mapping used to create them. Any decode error is an
   276	                // internal codec bug or memory corruption. Keep this switch
   277	                // exhaustive so new decoder errors require classification.
   278	                switch (err) {
   279	                    error.TruncatedInput,
   280	                    error.InvalidOffset,
   281	                    error.OutputTooSmall,
   282	                    error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   283	                    => {},
   284	                }
   285	
   286	                log.err("failed to restore compressed page err={}", .{err});
   287	                @panic("failed to restore compressed terminal page");
   288	            },
   289	
   290	            .discard => compressed.page,
   291	        };
   292	
   293	        // Remove our compressed data
   294	        compressed.deinit();
   295	
   296	        // We're now a resident, non-compressed node.
   297	        self.data = .{ .resident = restored };
   298	        return &self.data.resident;
   299	    }
   300	
   301	    inline fn isCompressed(self: *const Node) bool {
   302	        return switch (self.data) {
   303	            .resident => false,
   304	            .compressed => true,
   305	        };
   306	    }
   307	};
   260	
   261	    // Left/right scroll regions.
   262	    // Precondition: right > left
   263	    // Precondition: right <= cols - 1
   264	    left: size.CellCountInt,
   265	    right: size.CellCountInt,
   266	};
   267	
   268	/// Terminal-level cursor state shared by all screens.
   269	pub const Cursor = struct {
   270	    /// Whether the current cursor appearance follows the configured defaults.
   271	    is_default: bool = true,
   272	
   273	    /// Configured style restored by DECSCUSR default, RIS and DECSTR.
   274	    default_style: Screen.CursorStyle = .block,
   275	
   276	    /// Configured blink restored by DECSCUSR default, RIS and DECSTR.
   277	    /// Null selects the terminal emulator default, which is blinking.
   278	    default_blink: ?bool = false,
   279	};
   280	
   281	pub const Options = struct {
   282	    /// The size of the terminal grid in cells. Both must be at least 1,
   283	    /// otherwise `init` returns `error.InvalidValue`.
   284	    cols: size.CellCountInt,
   285	    rows: size.CellCountInt,
